Headline: Wes Anderson: A Feature Film Timeline
Text:
Wes Anderson has spent three decades making precisely composed, symmetrical, pastel-toned films about families, misfits, and the stories people tell about themselves. This timeline follows every feature he has directed, from Bottle Rocket (1996) to The Phoenician Scheme (2025), plus the Oscar-winning short The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar.

Use the arrows or the timeline below to move between films. Colour bands mark four phases of his career, and each row groups films by format.

Headline: Bottle Rocket
Text:
Anderson's debut grew out of a 1994 black-and-white short of the same name that screened at Sundance. Three aimless friends in Texas plan an inept heist. It made little at the box office but became a cult favourite, and Martin Scorsese later named it one of his favourite films of the 1990s.

  • Distributor: Columbia Pictures
  • Written by: Wes Anderson & Owen Wilson
  • Starring: Luke Wilson, Owen Wilson, Robert Musgrave, James Caan

Headline: Rushmore
Text:
A precocious, overcommitted prep-school student (Jason Schwartzman, in his first film role) competes with a melancholy industrialist (Bill Murray) for the affection of a teacher. Anderson won the Independent Spirit Award for Best Director, and the film was added to the Library of Congress's National Film Registry in 2016.

  • Distributor: Touchstone Pictures
  • Written by: Wes Anderson & Owen Wilson
  • Starring: Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Olivia Williams

Headline: The Royal Tenenbaums
Text:
A family of faded child prodigies reunites when their estranged father claims to be dying. Gene Hackman won a Golden Globe for his performance, the screenplay was nominated for an Academy Award, and the film was Anderson's biggest box-office hit until The Grand Budapest Hotel.

  • Distributor: Touchstone Pictures
  • Written by: Wes Anderson & Owen Wilson
  • Starring: Gene Hackman, Anjelica Huston, Gwyneth Paltrow, Ben Stiller

Headline: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
Text:
Anderson's homage to Jacques Cousteau follows an oceanographer hunting the shark that ate his partner. Filmed at Cinecittà in Rome, it features stop-motion sea creatures by Henry Selick and Seu Jorge's Portuguese covers of David Bowie songs. It was his first film co-written with Noah Baumbach.

  • Distributor: Touchstone Pictures
  • Written by: Wes Anderson & Noah Baumbach
  • Starring: Bill Murray, Owen Wilson, Cate Blanchett, Anjelica Huston

Headline: The Darjeeling Limited
Text:
Three estranged brothers take a train journey across India a year after their father's death. Much of it was shot aboard a moving train in Rajasthan. The short Hotel Chevalier, starring Natalie Portman, serves as its prologue.

  • Distributor: Fox Searchlight Pictures
  • Written by: Wes Anderson, Roman Coppola & Jason Schwartzman
  • Starring: Owen Wilson, Adrien Brody, Jason Schwartzman

Headline: Fantastic Mr. Fox
Text:
Anderson's first stop-motion feature adapts Roald Dahl's children's book about a fox who can't give up stealing chickens. It was nominated for the Academy Awards for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Score (Alexandre Desplat).

  • Distributor: 20th Century Fox
  • Written by: Wes Anderson & Noah Baumbach
  • Voices: George Clooney, Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray

Headline: Moonrise Kingdom
Text:
Two twelve-year-olds run away together on a New England island in 1965, setting off a search by the adults around them. The film opened the 2012 Cannes Film Festival and earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Screenplay.

  • Distributor: Focus Features
  • Written by: Wes Anderson & Roman Coppola
  • Starring: Jared Gilman, Kara Hayward, Bruce Willis, Edward Norton, Bill Murray, Frances McDormand
Alt Text: Embedded YouTube video: trailer for Moonrise Kingdom

Headline: The Grand Budapest Hotel
Text:
The story of a legendary concierge and his lobby boy in a fictional interwar European republic, inspired by the writings of Stefan Zweig. It won the Grand Jury Prize at Berlin, received nine Academy Award nominations including Best Picture, and won four. It remains his most commercially successful film.

  • Distributor: Fox Searchlight Pictures
  • Story by: Wes Anderson & Hugo Guinness
  • Starring: Ralph Fiennes, Tony Revolori, Saoirse Ronan, Adrien Brody

Headline: Isle of Dogs
Text:
In a near-future Japan, all dogs are exiled to a garbage island and a boy sets out to find his own. Anderson's second stop-motion feature won him the Silver Bear for Best Director at Berlin and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature. Its portrayal of Japanese culture also drew criticism.

  • Distributor: Fox Searchlight Pictures
  • Story by: Wes Anderson, Roman Coppola, Jason Schwartzman & Kunichi Nomura
  • Voices: Koyu Rankin, Bryan Cranston, Edward Norton, Bill Murray, Scarlett Johansson

Headline: The French Dispatch
Text:
An anthology framed as the final issue of an American magazine's French bureau, with three stories modelled on The New Yorker's long-form journalism. Its premiere was pushed from 2020 to the 2021 Cannes Film Festival by the COVID-19 pandemic.

  • Distributor: Searchlight Pictures
  • Story by: Wes Anderson, Roman Coppola, Hugo Guinness & Jason Schwartzman
  • Starring: Benicio del Toro, Adrien Brody, Tilda Swinton, Frances McDormand, Timothée Chalamet, Jeffrey Wright
Alt Text: Embedded YouTube video: trailer for The French Dispatch

Headline: Asteroid City
Text:
A stargazing convention in a 1955 desert town is interrupted by a world-changing event. The story is presented as a play within a television broadcast. It competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2023.

  • Distributor: Focus Features
  • Story by: Wes Anderson & Roman Coppola
  • Starring: Jason Schwartzman, Scarlett Johansson, Tom Hanks, Jeffrey Wright
Alt Text: Embedded YouTube video: trailer for Asteroid City

Headline: The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar
Text:
A 39-minute adaptation of Roald Dahl's story about a rich man who learns to see without his eyes, and the first of four Dahl shorts Anderson made for Netflix. It won the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film in March 2024, Anderson's first Oscar win.

  • Distributor: Netflix
  • Written by: Wes Anderson, from the story by Roald Dahl
  • Starring: Benedict Cumberbatch, Ralph Fiennes, Dev Patel, Ben Kingsley

Headline: The Phoenician Scheme
Text:
A ruthless European industrialist names his estranged daughter, a novice nun, as heir to his business empire as assassins close in. It competed for the Palme d'Or at Cannes in 2025.

  • Distributor: Focus Features
  • Story by: Wes Anderson & Roman Coppola
  • Starring: Benicio del Toro, Mia Threapleton, Michael Cera
